interfaces.name: Microsoft 365 web client
interfaces.classification_rationale: Actions are expressed by manipulating views, menus and forms of a navigable representation of documents and mailboxes (Affordance Manipulation).

provenance.evidence: First-party web versions of Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, OneDrive.

interfaces.name: Microsoft 365 desktop client
interfaces.classification_rationale: First-party desktop apps whose actions are affordance manipulation of a navigable UI; distinct client surface, same Interactive paradigm.

provenance.evidence: Office desktop apps installed on Windows and Mac via Click-to-Run.

interfaces.name: Microsoft 365 mobile client
interfaces.classification_rationale: First-party mobile apps; Affordance Manipulation on a distinct mobile surface.

provenance.evidence: iOS and Android versions of Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneDrive, Outlook.

interfaces.name: Microsoft Graph REST API
interfaces.technology: REST/OData over HTTPS (graph.microsoft.com v1.0 and beta)
interfaces.classification_rationale: Consumer explicitly invokes provider-defined operations against resources via structured HTTP requests (Operation Invocation).

provenance.evidence: Structured {HTTP method} https://graph.microsoft.com/{version}/{resource} request pattern over M365 data.
Microsoft Graph is the unified REST API for Microsoft 365 services.

interfaces.name: Exchange Online administrative PowerShell
interfaces.classification_rationale: Explicit command invocation through cmdlets over a distinct Exchange endpoint and auth, separate primitive from Graph REST.

provenance.evidence: First-party command-line cmdlet interface with its own REST-backed connection to Exchange Online.

interfaces.name: Internet mail protocols (SMTP submission, IMAP, POP)
interfaces.technology: Authenticated SMTP, IMAP4, POP3 with OAuth 2.0
interfaces.classification_rationale: Structured protocol operations to send and retrieve mail against provider-defined Exchange Online endpoints (Operation Invocation).

provenance.evidence: Authenticated SMTP client submission for Office 365 / Microsoft 365 mailboxes.
OAuth support for IMAP, POP and SMTP for Microsoft 365 users.

interfaces.name: Microsoft Graph change notifications
interfaces.technology: Subscriptions delivered via webhooks, Azure Event Hubs, or Azure Event Grid
interfaces.classification_rationale: The service initiates delivery to a consumer-controlled receiver when a subscribed resource changes (Event Notification), not consumer-invoked.

provenance.evidence: Applications subscribe and receive service-initiated notifications via webhooks, Event Hubs, or Event Grid.
Graph POSTs change notifications to the consumer's notificationUrl endpoint.

interfaces.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer expresses intent through natural-language messages; tool, plugin and MCP orchestration is internal to the service (Contextual Conversation), matching the assistant-with-internal-tools boundary case.

provenance.evidence: Declarative agents let users ask in natural language; Copilot reasons over and invokes tools internally.
Copilot presented as an AI assistant across the Microsoft 365 apps.

interfaces.name: Microsoft MCP Server for Enterprise
interfaces.classification_rationale: Exposes semantically described Graph tools that agents discover and select via tools/list and tools/call as part of the interaction contract (Capability Discovery and Invocation), the MCP boundary case for Agentic rather than Programmatic.

provenance.evidence: First-party MCP endpoint exposing microsoft_graph_suggest_queries, microsoft_graph_get, microsoft_graph_list_properties for agent discovery and invocation. Preview; currently Entra identity read-only over Graph.

access_mechanism_ledger.detail: No first-party persistent navigable TUI; terminal access is command-based only (already classified as Programmatic).

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: CLI (Exchange Online and M365 admin PowerShell)
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: Exchange Online administrative PowerShell (Programmatic); Teams and SharePoint Online Management Shell share the cmdlet paradigm within this family.

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: Microsoft Graph SDKs and Graph PowerShell SDK
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: SDKs/client libraries and a wrapper over Graph REST; barred by the do-not-count rule.
First-party but a thin command wrapper over the Graph REST API, not a distinct contract.
Community/open-source project, not a provider-defined Microsoft interface.
First-party developer testing tool that issues Graph API requests; operations belong to the Graph REST API.
External integrations and data ingestion, not first-party access interfaces to the service.
